en: In the consecration of mango groves, gardens, and so forth, one should offer a directional *bali* offering. Then, identifying oneself with Vairocana, one should meditate on the principal tree as the form of Vairocana immediately following the realization of emptiness. Having caused the Jñānasattva Vairocana to enter it preceded by the offering of water for the feet (*argha*) and other rites, one should consecrate it with water from the ritual vase. One should then resolve that the tree transformed from that [deity], as well as the other trees, are likewise transformed. Having worshipped that principal tree and its presiding deity with flowers and other offerings, one should [offer] fruits and so forth for the sake of others.

Having requested [permission] from the deities of the directions for the sake of the long-term stability of the grove and so forth that one is constructing, one should offer the bali-oblations to those directions.

Regarding the ritual for the consecration of mango groves and the like: after offering the directional *bali* cakes, one should—identifying oneself as Vairocana—visualize the principal tree as Vairocana following the meditation on emptiness. Then, having invited the wisdom-being Vairocana preceded by the offering of water for the feet (*argha*) and other rites, [one should proceed].

One should perform the consecration with water from the vase; at that very moment, one should cultivate the firm conviction that that tree and all other trees have likewise undergone transformation. Then, one should offer worship with divine flowers and so forth, empowered by those principal trees.

Having requested that the groves and other such places which serve the welfare of others—such as those consisting of fruit trees and so forth—remain for a long time, one should offer the ritual cakes (bali) to the [eight] directions.
Thus concludes the procedure for the consecration of groves and similar sites.
Thus concludes the ritual for consecrating forest groves and the like.
In all these aforementioned procedures, the general rule is that if no mantra is specified for a particular rite, one should recite the *sārvakarmika-mantra* (the universal rite mantra).
It should be explained that in all these procedures for recitation, in whatever rite the mantra is not explicitly stated, the *sarvakarmika* (all-purpose) mantra is to be recited there.
